transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-11 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jia (Redwood SRE), Priya (Acme CTO), Liam (Lead ML Eng), Maya (Infra), Evan (Product)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya: hi priya here, liam, maya, evan with me
[00:11] Alex: great, alex and samir from redwood, jia on infra
[00:16] Samir: cool, agenda: run through the benchmark slides, dig into tail latency, and agree next steps

[03:02] Alex: ok slide one, median latency numbers — redwood with kv cache on, intelligent batching, we see median of ~110ms at 256 token seq for your sample prompt set, compared to baseline provider median ~160ms in their public config
[03:27] Liam: can i ask quick, are you measuring total walltime including network? the baseline numbers we have are from their hosted endpoint so yes network included
[03:36] Samir: correct, for parity we included a 50ms added network hop in the test harness to match your region
[04:02] Priya: the numbers look promising but our worry is the 99th pct — our SLAs care about that
[04:15] Jia: on the 99th we saw redwood at ~420ms with bursts, baseline provider around 380ms in their single-instance tests — however with redwood's autoscale and dedicated pools we can tune that down
[04:30] Maya: what's changing the tail so much, is it batching delays?
[04:34] Samir: yes partly, batching adds head-of-line wait, we adjusted batching window from 20ms to 10ms during this run, that improved median but can worsen tail if traffic is bursty without KV cache; enabling prefix/KV cache reduced repeated prefix cost a lot for your traffic which is chatty

[08:05] Evan: one more question on comparison — are model variants same? quantization levels?
[08:12] Alex: good question, we used the same open model family and a 4-bit quantized variant for both, but baseline provider ran on their internal optimizations which may include custom kernels; we matched seq length and batch sizes as closely as possible
[08:45] Liam: did you test the dedicated pool config? we care about predictable throughput more than cost for peak windows
[08:51] Samir: yes, dedicated GPU pool at N=4 (A10x4) gave us stable throughput 450 rps for your 128-token average request, latency median ~95ms, 99th ~320ms under steady load
[09:12] Priya: those dedicated numbers are attractive, what's the pricing delta vs baseline?
[09:20] Alex: i'll share a pricing sheet after this call — short answer: dedicated reserved capacity is higher nominally but per-token cost can be lower at scale when you factor batching and KV cache savings

[12:00] Maya: also security — we need KMS integration and audit logs, plus SSO with SAML, do you support customer-managed keys?
[12:10] Alex: yes for private deployments we integrate with KMS/HSM and we have audit logs and SSO; we'll attach SOC2 summary in the deck
[12:22] Priya: ok please include retention and log export formats

[15:30] Samir: walking through the microbench results — this is the 99th percentile under spike workload (80% of peak QPS for 30s then 20% idle). redwood default config 99th = 420ms; enable KV cache + smaller batching window -> 340ms; dedicated pool with prewarmed workers -> 310ms
[16:00] Liam: baseline provider claims 280ms 99th under their managed cluster, but we suspect they have more aggressive prewarming and different eviction policy
[16:18] Samir: right and also their published numbers sometimes exclude cold-starts; we can run a joint test against their endpoint if you want, but better is on-prem smoke test to reproduce network and infra

[20:05] Priya: latency aside, throughput numbers? we saw baseline provide 520 rps on our 128-token pattern, your dedicated config was 470 rps, is that correct?
[20:18] Samir: that's correct in that single-instance baseline; however horizontal scaling and our autoscaler hit 1200 rps across the pool with consistent 99th ~330ms, baseline provider would need additional nodes to match, which bumps cost
[20:40] Maya: can you share the raw throughput logs? we want to plug them into our cost model
[20:46] Samir: yes we'll share logs and the harness CSVs

[24:00] Evan: we noticed a couple of transcriptions where tokens are double-counted in your cost calc sheet last week — any explanation?
[24:15] Alex: thanks for flagging, that's on us, we had a tokenizer mismatch set to gpt-3 style vs cl100k, we'll normalize and resend updated cost calc

[27:30] Alex: small demo of tuning knobs — we lowered batch time threshold, enabled prefix cache for common greetings and templated prompts, that dropped per-token GPU time by ~15%
[28:05] Liam: that's great, can the cache be persisted across restarts?
[28:12] Jia: yes KV cache is warmable and we can snapshot and restore cache state for dedicated/private setups, on hosted it is warmed via traffic and optional seed lists

[31:50] Maya: about on-prem — our legal team requires an air-gapped option for one environment, timeline is tight for proof-of-concept, can you support a smoke test on our hardware next month?
[32:05] Alex: yes we can do a smoke test, jia will coordinate host configs and a short SRE runbook
[32:12] Jia: i'll prepare a runbook, need your host specs and network topology

[36:00] Priya: can you also run a 99th percentile test that mimics our bursty traffic early morning ramp? we want to see worst-case tail
[36:10] Samir: yes we'll script a worn-in burst workload, capture CPU/GPU metrics, and send the raw traces

[40:22] Evan: any regulatory red flags we should call out now?
[40:28] Alex: SOC2 in place, we have customer-managed KMS in private mode, data residency options per region, and we log everything for audits — will share SOC2 report and the compliance addendum

[44:00] Priya: ok recap — send pricing and reserved capacity options, run 99th pct microbench with your tuned config vs baseline endpoint, share raw logs and throughput CSVs, schedule on-prem smoke test week of 2026-03-23
[44:20] Alex: yep i'll follow up with an email and calendar invites, thanks everyone
[44:28] Liam: thanks all
[44:30] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributed short phrases and filler words; some product names in transcript may be slightly garbled (e.g., kvcache, k v cache, redwood-ded).
